# INDEX (index.archi)

> The global atlas of architects' registration bodies: sourced, dated headcounts
> for 180 countries — registration regime, title protection, public registers,
> open-data catalogue, A–D data-quality grades. Compilation CC BY 4.0,
> Edberg Porporty (EDBERG.archi). Not a directory of persons.

Key facts: the UIA claims 745,665 architects across 117 sections (Feb 2025)
without any per-country breakdown; this atlas is that breakdown. 88 headcounts
are sourced and dated; 25 countries are grade A (bulk-downloadable rosters),
55 grade B (searchable registers), 91 grade D (estimates only — treat as a
work plan, not a result). Japan's kenchikushi figure is flagged non-comparable
and excluded from sums.

## Data

- [atlas.json](https://index.archi/atlas.json): complete dataset (meta, 180
  countries, federations, open-data catalogue), JSON UTF-8, stable URL
- [DONNEES.md](https://index.archi/DONNEES.md): field-by-field schema (French),
  derived from the dataset — includes controlled vocabularies and counts
- [SOURCES.md](https://index.archi/SOURCES.md): one line per country with the
  primary source URL of each headcount

## Citation

- DOI (concept, always latest): **10.5281/zenodo.21819381**
- DOI (this version, v1.0.0): 10.5281/zenodo.21819382

  registres d'architectes". Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21819381
  (CC BY 4.0)

## Reading rules

- Counts are REGISTERED architects at the official body — never graduates,
  never de-facto practitioners; jurisdictions compare only on that basis.
- Every figure carries `effectif_source_url`, `effectif_annee`,
  `effectif_nature` and a `qualite` grade — quote them with the number.
- Entries with `hors_echelle` are real but non-comparable: keep them out of
  sums, say why (the field carries the reason).
- No personal data here: name lists stay with their publishers (see the
  `catalogue` block for links).
